deviations: Instruments: the raw effective prices of potatoes/water/fuel are missing for ~1/3 of households; to keep the same N in all eight columns (as the paper states) the filled-in series lnPRE_*_ shipped in the analysis data (deflated, gaps filled with cell averages) are used, converted back to nominal logs by adding IP (equal to lnp_* wherever the household purchased).

LIML has no fixest/ivreg implementation; it is computed as a k-class estimator on variables partialled out on the exogenous regressors (and household FE via fixest), with exogenous coefficients (incl. T) recovered by regressing y - beta*lnp on the exogenous set. Only point estimates are computed for the IV columns (no SEs).

Sample: the T2 panel (25,775 rows, Aug 2011-Apr 2014) with listwise deletion on all regression variables; economic situation (SITUACTHOG_j) is missing for 4,445 rows, giving 20,872 obs / 10,729 households (586 singleton households; fixest drops them in FE columns, which does not change FE coefficients; reported N and household count include them, as Stata xtreg would).
notes: Spec (eq. 4): ln y on Reform T (T2), ln(price kWh) (lnp_kwh), ln income and its square (lny, lny2), months since reform (dist), controls (household size, rooms, m2, elderly, education dummies, economic-situation dummies, renting, building >25y, municipality-size dummies, urban, province-capital dummies, region dummies), quarter dummies and year FE; household FE in cols 3/4/7/8; household-clustered SEs. T2 was taken as T because its non-missing sample is exactly the paper's 25,775-observation panel. Because the price is defined as expenditure/consumption, ln expenditure = ln consumption + ln price exactly in this data, so every expenditure Reform coefficient equals its consumption counterpart (and the price coefficient is shifted by +1); the paper reports them as different, which this data cannot reproduce with these definitions.
